newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba member doubts rate cut could fuel demand.
newsitem.headline: Buba member doubts rate cut could fuel demand.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said he doubted that lowering German interest rates would spark the demand necessary to boost the economy, a German newspaper reported.
In a release ahead of publication on Wednesday, the Berliner Zeitung said Kuehbacher did not think domestic investment would be boosted by a cut in interest rates.
"The demand markets are simply not there," the paper quoted Kuehbacher as saying in a summary of an interview. In many European countries, capital investment was strong, but not in Germany, he said.
Kuehbacher said investment would only rise when industry was more certain about the future, for example about the government's planned tax reforms.
He said the tax reform debate left companies uncertain about the future and urged the government to finalise the reforms before the summer break so investment could pick up by the end of the year.
Kuehbacher said if the reforms were not finalised, the country's unemployment -- already at a record high of 4.7 million -- would continue to climb. (( --Bonn Newsroom, +49 228 26097160))
